notes: Interaction performance: navigation no longer waits for a page's data. The router starts every navigation immediately and only the newest one may paint, so a click during a slow request is honoured instead of being swallowed (previously `if (isNavigating) return` dropped every click until the previous page finished loading).

Requests belong to the page that started them: leaving a page aborts its in-flight calls (AbortController) and a late response can never overwrite the page you are on. Cancelled requests are reported as cancelled, never as a backend failure or an error toast.

Read cache with request de-duplication (frontend/js/api.js): collection reads are cached for API_CACHE_TTL_MS (20 s), identical concurrent reads share one request, every write and every 'datasets/models/training changed' event invalidates the cache, and a manual Refresh bypasses it. Measured: 30 API calls per navigation cycle before, 9 now, 4 on a repeat cycle.

Large lists render in bounded pages (frontend/js/components.js renderPagedList) with one delegated listener instead of one per row, and list cards no longer register AOS observers. Measured on 300 models / 500 datasets: Models page 1089 ms → 178 ms, Datasets 858 ms → 104 ms, DOM 19 435 → 1 094 nodes.

Instant press feedback and duplicate-action protection: a delegated pointerdown listener shows .is-pressed before any handler runs, buttons show a spinner via aria-busy, and start/pause/resume/stop/create actions run once even if tapped repeatedly.

Live training metrics are coalesced into one animation frame (log lines, tiles and both charts flush once per frame instead of once per metric event), the log panel is capped at 300 lines, live charts update without the 800 ms entry animation, and leaving the Training page destroys its Chart.js instances.
Startup: Chart.js, SweetAlert2, Supabase and AOS are deferred (off the parser's critical path) and the chart helpers degrade gracefully if Chart.js is unavailable.

Backend: objective 'newest N' windows for training metrics and logs (?limit=), so a long run no longer streams its entire history on every poll (600 steps: 75 KB → 25 KB); payloads and latency are guarded by backend/tests/test_api_performance.py.

Performance instrumentation (frontend/js/perf.js): first paint, DOMContentLoaded/load, time-to-interactive, per-route navigation time, per-endpoint API latency, long tasks, memory, failures and cache size — via CORPUS_PERF.snapshot()/print(), CORPUS_APP.getDiagnostics().perf, or ?debug=1. Route paths only; no tokens, headers or user data.

Reproducible measurement tooling: scripts/perf-probe.mjs (simulated backend latency + payload size, real router and page modules) and frontend/tests/performance.test.mjs (12 regression tests for the behaviours above).
howToVerify: GET <frontend-url>/version.json — the deployed buildId must equal the buildId committed in frontend/version.json on main.
